paragraphs.source_en: On the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month of Keichō 3, Ishida Mitsunari set out for Hakata, accompanied by Asano Nagamasa and Mōri Hidemoto. It was as though people had long been waiting impatiently for this moment: no sooner had Mitsunari departed than visitors to Tokugawa Ieyasu's residence in Fushimi suddenly multiplied. They included not only the families of commanders serving in Korea, but even court nobles and monks bearing gifts. Ieyasu treated these visitors with all possible gravity, for he understood perfectly well why they had come.
